messages.content: Compare candidate A and candidate B symmetrically for the stated vacancy and employer preferences. Choose A or B only when known facts support a material preference. Skill levels are integers 0..7; compare skill levels separately from evidence reliability. Grade is the formal test result; a role or free-text narrative does not reassign grade. Confirmed, partial, self_reported, and pending are different evidence states: uncertainty reduces certainty without erasing declared skills. Null duration_months and production_support are unknown, never zero months or false. Use only explicit technical requirements; do not invent technical minima. A class-only vacancy has no unstated technical requirements, and missing facts are not a negative qualification. Use salary overlap as an eligibility constraint only when the declared vacancy requires it. Salary affects preference only when the employer explicitly mentions it. Do not invent salary thresholds or a minimum technical fit. Salary economy, when explicitly requested, must be weighed against known technical fit; cheaper does not automatically defeat stronger fit. When unknown tradeoffs prevent a justified preference, use tie for a supported comparable fit or insufficient for uncertainty that prevents comparison. Tie means genuine comparable suitability supported by available facts; insufficient means the facts do not support a comparison. Swapping A and B must swap A/B labels and preserve tie/insufficient. Candidate position must never be a preference factor. Return JSON only: label, rationale, evidence, uncertainties. Rationale is one short sentence of at most 160 characters. Evidence is 2 to 4 exact strings copied from available_citations; never reconstruct or edit a citation. A/B labels require at least one citation per candidate. Use at most two short uncertainties. Tie/insufficient are legitimate answers. Do not report confidence or probabilities.
